ground_truth.description: _claimFees() sweeps the entire balance of `token0`/`token1` after `collectFees()`, stealing rewards if `rewardToken` matches `token0` or `token1`. Impact: Bribe contract receives staking rewards instead of fees.
ground_truth.root_cause: _claimFees() sweeps the entire balance of `token0`/`token1` after `collectFees()`, stealing rewards if `rewardToken` matches `token0` or `token1`. Impact: Bribe contract receives staking rewards instead of fees.
ground_truth.attack_scenario: A test deposits 10 HYBR rewards, adds 0.1 HYBR fees, and `claimFees()` sweeps all 10.1 HYBR to the bribe contract.
ground_truth.fix_description: Transfer only the difference in balance before/after `collectFees()`; add access control to `claimFees`. Status: Mitigation confirmed.

vulnerabilities.explanation: The _claimFees() function sweeps the entire balance of token0/token1 after calling collectFees(), without distinguishing between fee tokens and reward tokens. If rewardToken matches token0 or token1, staking rewards will be incorrectly transferred to the bribe contract instead of being distributed to stakers.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: 1. Reward token is same as token0 (e.g., HYBR). 2. Stakers deposit liquidity and earn rewards. 3. Anyone calls claimFees(). 4. Function collects fees via collectFees(), then sweeps ALL token0 balance. 5. Staking rewards (not just fees) are sent to internal_bribe contract. 6. Stakers lose their earned rewards.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Track token balances before and after collectFees(): uint256 balanceBefore0 = IERC20(_token0).balanceOf(address(this)); uint256 balanceBefore1 = IERC20(_token1).balanceOf(address(this)); clPool.collectFees(); claimed0 = IERC20(_token0).balanceOf(address(this)) - balanceBefore0; claimed1 = IERC20(_token1).balanceOf(address(this)) - balanceBefore1;

prediction.overall_explanation: The contract contains one critical vulnerability where staking rewards can be stolen when reward tokens match pool tokens. The _claimFees() function incorrectly transfers the entire token balance instead of only the collected fees. This is a concrete, exploitable vulnerability that doesn't require admin compromise. Other functions appear properly secured with reentrancy guards and access controls.
